objectives.observation: The trunk is pale silvery grey and looks even-toned, with no deep furrows or plates visible. At this distance the bark texture cannot be resolved, so smoothness is only inferred from the uniform tone and outline.

There is one straight, fairly slender bole with no major branches for roughly the lower 40% of the tree's height, from the ground to about the fork. The only exception is a short, bare, horizontal branch or stub on the left side just below the fork.

The bole splits into two main ascending leaders in a narrow V at about 40-45% of the tree's height. The left leader bends and kinks slightly. Both leaders divide repeatedly into ascending, then outward-spreading, scaffold limbs.

The crown is broad and dome-shaped to flat-topped, and much wider than the trunk's clear height. It occupies roughly the upper 55-60% of the tree and is about as wide as the crown is tall, or slightly wider. The outline is rounded and scalloped rather than conical.
Dark limbs, visible through the foliage, rise steeply from the fork and then fan outward. Toward the crown edge they arch to near-horizontal and slightly droop, especially on the right side.
Leaves sit in fine, flat-to-drooping sprays along slender twigs. This gives the crown edge a feathery, lacy, layered texture, with individual spray tips standing out against the sky.
The crown is fairly open. Sky and the internal branch structure show through across much of it, and the foliage looks like many small clusters rather than one solid mass.
Individual leaf shape, margin and venation cannot be resolved at this viewing distance, so no leaf-level traits can be confirmed.
The base of the trunk flares slightly and looks darker, possibly from moss, staining or shadow. The cause cannot be determined.

defects: Both seeds render a narrow columnar crown with a pointed top, like a Lombardy poplar. The crown is about 2.5-3x taller than it is wide. The reference shows a broad, domed to flat-topped crown that is about as wide as it is tall.
Foliage starts about 10-15% up the tree in both seeds. The reference has a clear, branch-free bole for about 40% of its height.
The trunk splits low, at about 10-15% of the height, into three or more steep, near-parallel stems. The reference splits into two co-dominant leaders in a narrow V at about 40-45% of the height.
The limbs stay steeply upright up to the crown edge. They never fan outward or arch to near-horizontal and droop, as the reference limbs do.
The crown edge is a uniform fuzzy fringe of upright foliage. It lacks the reference's flat-to-drooping, layered sprays with individual spray tips standing out against the sky.
The foliage is a dense, mostly solid mass. Little sky or internal branch structure shows through, whereas the reference crown is open and translucent.

findings.observation: Crown silhouette: both renders show a tall, narrow column with a pointed top (width about 0.35-0.4 of height). The reference crown is broad and domed, about as wide as it is tall or wider.
The clear bole ends at about 10-15% of the tree's height in both renders, versus about 40% in the reference.
Both renders split low into several steep, parallel stems. Neither shows a two-leader narrow V at 40-45% of the height.
The visible pale limbs in the renders stay steeply ascending all the way to the crown edge, with no outward arching or droop. The reference's dark limbs fan out and droop near the edge.
The render crown edge is fine-grained but upright and uniform. It does not show the reference's layered, drooping sprays.
The render crowns are dense and mostly opaque. The reference crown is open, with sky and branches visible throughout.
Leaf shape cannot be resolved in the reference or at the renders' viewing distance, so there is no basis for comparison.
The render foliage is mid-to-bright green rather than the reference's pale yellow-green. The inventory classes leaf colour as seasonal variation.
The render crowns are nearly symmetric, while the reference is right-heavy. The inventory classes this asymmetry as variation.
